To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
advanced optical modulation formats are an important ingredient to the design and operation of modern high-speed optical networks.
advanced modulation formats can provide significant capacity increases in high-capacity optical networks, and that they can do so while maintaining high spectral efficiencies.
the following modulation formats can be used to increase the capacity of a fiber link: QPSK, 8-PSK, 16-QAM, 64-QAM, and 256-QAM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and analysis of optical communication systems based on advanced optical modulation formats, such as phase-shift-keying, polarization modulation and coherent detection.
the generation and detection techniques for advanced modulation formats and the study of their resilience to the impairments found in modern optical networking systems.
the design and implementation of advanced optical modulation formats for high capacity optical transport networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the future will be a combination of the above mentioned modulation formats and that the choice of the most appropriate format will depend on the specific requirements of the application and on the specific characteristics of the optical transmission system.
the optical modulation format is the most important factor in determining the maximum transmission distance of an optical fiber communication system.
the future of high capacity optical transport networks will be dominated by the use of advanced optical modulation formats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of multigigahertz modulation formats in WDM optical networks is a promising solution to the capacity crunch.
the optical communication industry has made a major shift from using on-off keying (OOK) to more advanced modulation formats.
the optical modulation formats are the most critical element for the design of future optical networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of multigigahertz bandwidth modulators and coherent detection can enable the transmission of high capacity signals over long distances, with the potential to increase the capacity of a single wavelength by orders of magnitude.

advanced modulation formats can be generated and detected in a robust and reliable fashion using standard optical components, and that the performance of these systems can be accurately predicted by numerical modeling and experimentally characterized using a variety of techniques.
multigigabit per second intensity modulated formats can be generated and detected at high spectral efficiency with a low cost and complexity.
